Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Adult female with several days of constant, worsening lower abdominal (midline, below umbilicus) pain, severity ~8/10, associated with light pink vaginal spotting and slight discharge, and nausea without vomiting. Last menstrual period ~2–3 weeks ago. Sexually active; contraceptive implant in situ ~1 year; last pregnancy test ~1 month ago. No fever, syncope, dyspnea, or shoulder-tip pain reported. Prior constipation last week now resolved. Denies dysuria; urinary frequency unclear.
- Differential considerations consistent with DDx:
  - Ectopic pregnancy (Medium likelihood): Pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting; pregnancy status unknown and implant does not eliminate risk. Must be excluded urgently.
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease (Medium likelihood): Lower abdominal pain with abnormal bleeding/spotting and slight discharge in a sexually active patient; absence of fever does not exclude.
  - Functional ovarian cyst/ruptured cyst (Medium likelihood): Acute pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting; implant use can be associated with functional cysts.
  - Other lower-likelihood considerations per DDx: Appendicitis (low–medium), UTI (low).
- Plan from visit: Arrange prompt face-to-face clinic evaluation for abdominal (and likely pelvic) examination. Perform a pregnancy test today; if positive, seek urgent evaluation. Safety netting provided for worsening pain, inability to keep fluids down, or other concerning symptoms.

Management Plan
- Patient to call support line to arrange in-person clinic appointment for examination.
- Urine pregnancy test to be performed today; if positive, patient to contact clinic immediately for urgent assessment.
- Return/seek urgent care if pain worsens significantly, new concerning symptoms develop (e.g., dizziness/syncope, shoulder pain, heavy bleeding), or unable to tolerate fluids.
- Additional management/referrals not recorded.

- Pathology tests as above: Urine pregnancy test today; further labs (e.g., CBC, inflammatory markers, urinalysis, STI testing) not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Ectopic pregnancy (Medium): Pelvic pain and light vaginal spotting; sexually active with implant; no pregnancy test since symptom onset; must be excluded urgently.
- Pelvic inflammatory disease (Medium): Lower abdominal pain with abnormal bleeding/spotting and slight discharge in a sexually active patient; fever absent but not required.
- Functional ovarian cyst/ruptured cyst (Medium): Acute pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting; possible association with implant use.
